sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Media Relations and Crisis Public Relations Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — English Common Law and French Civil Law jointly applicable (bipodial system), with recognition of customary law; Bislama is the national language
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Vanuatu and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 2006, in force)

Agreement between the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Government of the Republic of Vanuatu for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 1998)
Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of the Republic of Vanuatu for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 1988)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus), 2017 (trade and investment facilitation framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act [Cap. 77] of 1993, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act No. 5 of 2019 (mandating registered agents to identify, verify and maintain beneficial ownership records); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 42 of 2018 (AML/CFT Act), ss. 55-62 (customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification, record-keeping and reporting to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit); Financial Dealers Licensing Act [Cap. 70]; Companies Act [Cap. 191]; VFSC Registered Agent Compliance Guidelines and VFIU directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each proposed shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country licensed notary public (based on original passport)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Vanuatu is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; foreign public documents must be legalized through a Vanuatu diplomatic/consular post in the country of origin or via the Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and External Trade)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each UBO and director (bank statement or utility bill not older than 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin-country bank or utility provider, then notarized by a licensed notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional bank reference letter addressed to the VFSC-licensed registered agent
Certificate of Incumbency or corporate register extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or licensed registered agent of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Charter, articles of incorporation or constitutive deed of any corporate shareholder (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar of the origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, and the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (VFIU) sanctions and warning lists; explicit PEP status declaration in the CDD questionnaire; automatic enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval for any PEP, politically exposed family member, or high-risk jurisdiction nexus; adverse hits require referral to the VFSC-licensed registered agent's AML/CFT compliance officer and possible filing of a suspicious transaction report with the VFIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Online Registry Portal (VFSC Corporate Registry, www.vfsc.vu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Roman/Latin script. English and French are the statutory drafting languages and are preferred for International Company names; Bislama names are generally not accepted for ICs. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into an English/French Latin-alphabet equivalent and must be distinguishable from all existing registered names. Names must end with a recognized suffix: 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Corp', 'Incorporated', 'Inc', 'Société Anonyme', or 'Pty Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name clearance refusal, the applicant must instruct its VFSC-licensed registered agent to file a written administrative reconsideration application with the VFSC Companies Registry within 14 business days, citing the name-availability search reference and addressing the stated ground of refusal (confusing similarity or restricted/sensitive token). If the Registry upholds the rejection, the applicant may, within 30 days of the final administrative decision, apply to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu for judicial review. In practice, submitting two alternative names in the same clearance cycle is the recommended mitigation strategy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for statutory purposes. An International Company must maintain a statutory registered office in Vanuatu at the address of its VFSC-licensed registered agent; a physical trading branch is not legally required for an overseas media relations and crisis PR agency. However, for corporate bank account opening, correspondent-bank vetting, and CRS/FATCA substance expectations, a physical or presence-based office is strongly recommended. A purely virtual-office model materially increases bank KYC rejection risk and may attract tax-residency and anti-abuse scrutiny in foreign revenue jurisdictions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate — approximately 25-35% probability of an unannounced VFSC or VFIU inspection of the licensed registered agent's premises within a 12-month compliance cycle; unannounced inspection risk directly targeting the IC's actual overseas PR trading premises is low, estimated below 10%, given the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier and the absence of a statutory licensing requirement for this industry.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: VFSC name availability search and clearance fee
VFSC International Company incorporation registration fee (standard authorized capital band)
Licensed registered agent and registered office establishment fee (IC Act [Cap. 77] section 19 compliant)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Vanuatu International Company formation practitioners

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO, PEP and sanctions screening package (UN/OFAC/HMT/VFIU lists plus beneficial ownership record file set-up)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per VFIU-aligned registered agent compliance fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization bundle in country of origin (passport, proof of address, bank reference for each UBO/director)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market notarial tariff in the principal's jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of corporate and personal documentation for Vanuatu filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and External Trade / Vanuatu consular post in the country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank professional reference letter preparation and courier dispatch (per signatory/UBO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service charge and prevailing courier benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act No. 32 of 1992 (Cap. 222), Republic of Vanuatu – Part II (Incorporation and Powers, ss. 5–12), Part III (Share Capital, ss. 13–19), Part IV (Registered Office and Registered Agent, ss. 20–22), and Part V (Directors, Officers, and Records, ss. 23–34)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division, Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (VFSC Form IC-1) together with Declaration of Compliance for Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or capital deposit account requirement. The International Company may be incorporated with zero issued capital and may denominate shares in any currency selected by the subscriber.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, as approved for filing with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222], be and are hereby adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER that the allotment and issue of [___] ordinary shares of no par value to the subscriber(s) be and is hereby ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be established at [Registered Office Address], Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu, and that [Registered Agent Name] be and is hereby appointed registered agent to maintain statutory records. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be appointed Director and [Name] be appointed Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until removed by resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Chairman be authorized to execute all statutory filings and pay all VFSC fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division – online name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed company names in order of preference via the VFSC e-registry or through a licensed registered agent. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing international company, must not contain restricted words (e.g. 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance') unless sector-licensed, and must end with the words 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or the abbreviation 'Ltd'.
required_dossiers: Copy of identification of each proposed shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, select a substitute from the reservation list within 5 business days or file a written request for administrative review of the refusal with the VFSC Registry Manager; priority of reservation shall not lapse if a compliant alternative is tendered within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Vanuatu registered agent; execution by all subscribers before a notary or via attested electronic signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Memorandum of Association (object clause, share structure, registered agent clause) and Articles of Association (director powers, meetings, indemnity, share transfer provisions). Each subscriber must affix signature witnessed by an independent adult; a Declaration of Compliance confirming compliance with the International Companies Act must be countersigned by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Subscriber identification (passport or national ID) and proof of address
Consent to act as registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the VFSC flags drafting defects, the registered agent shall amend the documents and re-execute within 7 business days; correction notices do not attract penalty if resolved before the statutory incorporation deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Filing to VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – Companies Registry Division, Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Memorandum and Articles, Declaration of Compliance, registered agent consent, and prescribed incorporation fee via the VFSC counter or e-registry. The registered agent shall retain a file copy and issue a receipt bearing the VFSC file number. The Registrar must issue a Certificate of Incorporation within the statutory review window unless the application is defective.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where VFSC issues a requisition or query, the registered agent must answer in writing and submit corrective documentation within 14 days; failure to cure may be appealed to the VFSC Registry Manager, with ultimate administrative review by the Minister responsible for financial services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – Registry Division; board of directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction of all filing requirements, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number. The first board resolution then allots shares, adopts the registered office address, and appoints officers. Where no share premium applies, the Company may issue subscriber shares at par or no par value and record allotment in the Register of Members within 21 days.
required_dossiers: Register of Members and allotment records
Consent forms of directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains clerical errors, petition VFSC for a rectification certificate; if the directors' consents are defective, reconvene the board and file corrected consents without lapse of the Company's existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and registered office of the International Company, Port Vila, Vanuatu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges, and beneficial owners) at the registered office; file annual confirmation and pay annual licence fee to VFSC; maintain board minutes and share transfer records; appoint a Money Laundering Reporting Officer where the Company carries out any financial activity, and adopt an AML/CFT risk assessment commensurate with the Low_Risk_Standard rating of the PR services business.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon non-compliance notice from VFSC, file all outstanding annual confirmations and pay any late fees within 30 days to avoid striking-off; seek reinstatement under the Act if the Company is struck off inadvertently.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Tourism, Industry and Commerce – Department of Industry (for general municipal business licence only if a physical office in Vanuatu is opened); no sector-competent regulator applies to international PR services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Vanuatu Business Licence under the Business Licence Act [Cap. 245] – not mandatory for an International Company that conducts all business outside Vanuatu and maintains only a registered agent address; a municipal business licence is required only where the Company leases physical premises or employs staff within Vanuatu

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change, Government of the Republic of Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Low-Risk Registration – office-based public relations and communications activity generates no significant environmental impact; no full EIA Report required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Where an office is maintained, sanitary wastewater must comply with the Waste Management Act [Cap. 280] and DEPC effluent guidelines for domestic sewage discharge; no VOC or industrial air emission thresholds apply; waste electrical and electronic equipment and paper waste must be disposed of through licensed waste operators; any stormwater discharge must not cause pollution to adjacent land or watercourses.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services for any leased office premises, including means-of-escape inspection and fire extinguisher placement per NFPA 10; structural load and occupancy verification/clearance from the Public Works Department for leased premises; workplace health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act for any locally engaged staff; no civil defense or clearance obligations apply where the Company operates solely through its registered agent without physical occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue Authority (VRA) — official tax and VAT administrator; portal: https://www.vra.gov.vu. Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — company registry and international company licensing; portal: https://www.vfsc.vu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) must first be incorporated under the International Companies Act through VFSC. If the IC makes taxable supplies in Vanuatu, it must apply for VAT/TIN registration with the VRA by submitting the VAT registration application form, certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, beneficial ownership identification, and physical address confirmation. VRA issues a TIN/VAT ID upon approval. An IC that does not make local taxable supplies has no mandatory TIN requirement; a Tax Exemption Certificate may be obtained from VFSC for statutory exemption documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — International Company is exempt from Vanuatu corporate income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, and stamp duty on offshore income; it is not subject to entity-level tax unless it makes taxable supplies in Vanuatu that trigger VAT obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime exists under Vanuatu law. Statutory elections are limited to optional VAT registration for small businesses and the voluntary application for a VFSC Tax Exemption Certificate. No partnership or transparent-entity elections are provided.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act [CAP 108]
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VUV 2,000,000 (VT 2,000,000) annual taxable turnover in Vanuatu triggers compulsory VAT registration; voluntary registration is permitted for entities making zero-rated export supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate exists in Vanuatu. VAT-registered businesses must issue sequential tax invoices with statutory particulars; invoices may be paper or electronic. VRA encourages electronic filing through its online portal but does not require government API integration or pre-clearance of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Vanuatu are zero-rated provided proof of export is obtained. Services, including public relations, media communication and advisory work performed for non-resident clients, are zero-rated where the recipient belongs outside Vanuatu, the services are supplied for use or benefit wholly outside Vanuatu, and there is no connection with taxable supplies in Vanuatu.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for physical goods; not required for pure services)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (where physical PR collateral, media kits, or printed matter is shipped)
Inward Remittance Certificate from a Vanuatu bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
VAT zero-rated export invoice with non-resident customer declaration and underlying service contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The VRA may conduct a retrospective audit of zero-rated export claims; if documentation is deficient or the export is determined to be a local supply, VAT at 12.5% is clawed back with statutory interest and penalties up to 200% of the unpaid tax. Fraudulent zero-rating may attract criminal fines of up to VUV 500,000, director disqualification, and imprisonment for up to 7 years; records must be retained for at least 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu maintains a liberalised exchange control regime under the Exchange Control Act [Cap. 112] administered by the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, qualified by only formal notification and transparency obligations for cross-border transfers exceeding VUV 10 million. Current account transactions are fully convertible; capital account transactions, including direct investment, portfolio investment, and profit remittance, are freely permitted with no prior approval for ICs enjoying tax-exempt status. Profit remittance hurdles are practically non-existent for a licensed International Company; however, the receiving financial institution may request underlying contracts, invoices, and proof of source of funds to comply with VUV anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism obligations. Statutory withholding tax does not apply to non-resident ICs, and dividends, royalties, and service fees can be repatriated in full without conversion restrictions. No surrender rules apply to export proceeds; the exporter may retain foreign currency in offshore or resident accounts.

stage_4.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Receipts from export transactions may be retained in foreign currency in any authorised dealer bank account (onshore or offshore) for an indefinite period. The only statutory requirement is that all goods/services exports must be declared on the RBV's reportable transaction monitoring forms when the value exceeds VUV 10 million per transaction, solely for statistical and suspicious-transaction detection purposes. This fully accommodates the overseas PR communication firm's retainer-based export model.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM with legal constraints. Offshore digital EMI platforms that have no physical presence in Vanuatu are not locally licensed by the VFSC or the RBV. They can only be used for non-resident liquidity purposes if the entity maintains a parallel domestic correspondent clearing capability. The RBV does not recognise such EMIs as authorised dealers in VUV, so any VUV clearing must route through a resident commercial bank. For a USD/EUR/AUD-denominated international PR agency, established EMIs such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, or MultiPass are legally acceptable for non-VUV treasury consolidation, provided they satisfy 3rd-party AML/KYC due diligence and the beneficial ownership documentation is aligned with VFSC records. Cross-border EMI accounts cannot be used as the sole bank account for statutory annual returns or for any transaction requiring VUV settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under current Vanuatu AML/CFT Regulations and the Financial Institutions Act, onboarding for International Companies is predominantly performed remotely. A physical appearance of all directors is not mandatory; however, each director and ultimate beneficial owner must undergo video-identified KYC through the bank's approved remote onboarding platform. The registered office service provider in Vanuatu (registered agent) must act as the introducer and must certify the corporate existence, full beneficial ownership chain, and signatory powers. In practice, a physical visit to Port Vila is advisable only where the bank's risk score for the jurisdiction of the beneficial owner is higher than low-risk or when a correspondent bank imposes enhanced due diligence. For the identified jurisdiction (VU) and low-risk business scope, remote onboarding is achievable within 7-12 working days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity where nominee shareholders or trusts are used
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent declaration of beneficial ownership, trust deed or nomination agreement, passport copies and proof of residential address of all UBOs exceeding 10% economic interest, certificate of Good Standing from VFSC, and a signed Risk Assessment Questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth concerns from initial capital injection originating from a non-transparent jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from the sending institution for 6 months, sworn source of wealth declaration, signed audit/commercial contracts evidencing rendering of PR services, and a copy of the sender's regulatory licence or professional registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEPS screening hit against a shareholder, director, or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent World-Check or Dow Jones screening report, explanation letter with countersigned declaration, legal opinion from Vanuatu counsel confirming no exposure to OFAC/EU/UN sanctions, and disqualification or clearance certificate from VFSC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared business activity and transaction pattern (high-volume cross-border retainers without supporting contracts)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master services agreement for global PR and media relations, client retainer schedule, monthly timesheets / deliverables reports, invoice log with ISIC 7310–classified scope, and an AML officer-approved transaction profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore digital EMIs as the principal receiving bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal memo confirming EMIs are not authorised dealers under VU law, a written account usage policy, the EMI's KYC file, and proof that a domestic correspondent account is maintained for VUV or emergency settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols for initial share capital must be routed via SWIFT to an authorised dealer bank in Vanuatu (e.g., ANZ or BSP) using purpose code 'G301 - Direct Investment' (or its local equivalent) when exceeding VUV 10 million. The remitting bank must include full legal name of the IC, BIC of the receiving bank, and both the sending and receiving account numbers. Supporting documents, including the share subscription resolution, bank confirmation of share proceeds, and RBV electronic declaration, must be transmitted to the receiving bank on the same business day. There is no minimum capital requirement for an International Company; a prudent initial injection of USD 20,000 is recommended to satisfy bank residual risk thresholds. No exchange control prior approval is needed; post-transaction filing is handled by the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements and operating expenses are executed through standard SWIFT MT103 over the correspondent banking network. For commercial LC transactions (e.g., procurement of production assets), the WC/BPU006 documentary credit via MT700 series is available through tier-1 banks. The firm may also use USD-AUD and EUR-VUV clearing corridors. Payments to overseas consultants and subcontractors must be supported by an executed service agreement, an invoice referencing ISIC 7310, and a settlement advice. The RSB reporting threshold of VUV 10 million applies; above this threshold, banks will pre-validate the transaction and attach the e-declaration receipt. No direct access to domestic RTGS (Central Clearing) system is provided to non-banking institutions; all settlements are bank-mediated.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanuatu vatu (VUV) outright forwards with a licensed dealer bank for currency exposure arising from cross-border retainer receipts
Cross-currency swaps between VUV and AUD/USD/EUR for treasury rebalancing, subject to underlying commercial exposure validation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore on VUV where the settlement is in USD, provided the onshore leg is arranged through a licensed commercial bank
Simple vanilla foreign exchange spot contracts with a settlement tenor not exceeding T+2

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee – International Company Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; a 30-day grace period applies before late-payment penalties accrue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late fee after 30 days; an additional 10% late fee accrues for each subsequent 90-day period; continued non-payment for approximately six months triggers administrative strike-off by VFSC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Certificate – Annual Register Audit Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: VFSC through the licensed Vanuatu registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation, coinciding with the registered agent's mandatory annual corporate register review.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct fine on the company, but the registered agent is subject to VFSC administrative sanctions and potential license revocation; agent resignation may lead to the company's involuntary strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Data Confirmation – AML/CFT Continuing Due Diligence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent maintaining the statutory registers (no public filing with VFSC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than 30 days following the anniversary date of incorporation, or promptly after any shareholder, director, or UBO change during the year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under Vanuatu's AML/CFT framework for failure to supply or validate UBO information; continued non-response may trigger a suspicious activity report to the Financial Intelligence Unit and agent resignation with consequent strike-off risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a Vanuatu International Company under the International Companies Act. An independent audit is required only if mandated by a shareholder resolution, a VFSC licence condition, or a bank/investment-prudential requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed statutory framework for International Companies; directors may adopt IFRS, IFRS for SMEs, or another reasonable accounting principle. Financial statements are not filed with VFSC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a register of members at the office of its licensed registered agent. Whenever ownership changes, the company must notify the registered agent and file updated share-transfer information with the agent. Annually, the agent must obtain a written confirmation of current UBO details, residential/professional addresses, and any share transfers; this confirmation is kept at the agent's office and is not a public filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (corporate resolutions and meeting records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (not required); voluntary certified audit quote: USD 2,500 – USD 8,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% - Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax; no Income Tax Act or CIT assessment regime exists in Vanuatu law.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies Act [Cap. 222], s.111 grants a permanent statutory exemption from all Vanuatu taxes, duties, and fees on income, assets, and transactions. Accordingly the effective CIT rate is 0%, with no capital gains tax, no payroll tax, no inheritance/estate duty, and no stamp duty on IC instruments issued in Vanuatu. The only recurring state charge is the VFSC annual licence fee, banded by authorised share capital. VAT at the prevailing standard rate (15% as amended effective 1 January 2024) applies solely to local supplies of goods/services in Vanuatu; an offshore PR/communication IC generating no local supplies has a 0% VAT burden.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No CIT return form or e-filing portal exists in Vanuatu. An International Company files nothing with Vanuatu Revenue and Customs (VRC) in respect of income. The only recurring state filing is the annual licence fee and annual return submitted by the registered agent through the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The VFSC annual licence fee is payable on the anniversary of incorporation of the IC; the registered agent in Port Vila must lodge the annual fee and the prescribed annual return before the anniversary date to avoid late fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC name, registration number, registered office, registered agent, director/shareholder names, authorised capital, and confirmation of s.111 exemption status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Beneficial ownership details of the foreign parent PR/communication firm must be current with the registered agent for AML/CDD purposes; no income, turnover, or asset declaration is made to any Vanuatu tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration that the IC has conducted no business with Vanuatu residents, owns no Vanuatu real estate, and remains outside the VAT net.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders may retain 100% ownership and all profits offshore with no Vanuatu tax return, but any unrelated Vanuatu-sourced PR services would convert the IC into a taxable local supply position under the VAT Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of the VFSC annual licence fee attracts a prescribed late fee plus continued accrual until payment; persistent non-payment results in administrative strike-off and dissolution under s.121 of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222], with consequent loss of the tax exemption and invalidation of contracts issued after dissolution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VAT Return (e-VAT 100) filed via the VRC e-Services portal (Vanuatu Revenue and Customs). Applicable only if the IC becomes VAT-registered by making taxable supplies in Vanuatu or if annual taxable turnover exceeds VUV 10,000,000 (approx. USD 85,000).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: VAT returns are due on or before the 20th day of the month following the end of the monthly tax period; nil returns are compulsory for all registered persons.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total value of taxable supplies (exclusive of VAT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave nil where the IC only invoices foreign clients for global PR, media relations, and crisis communication services; those export supplies are zero-rated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Output VAT chargeable on local supplies at the prevailing standard rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Charge VAT only on services physically supplied to Vanuatu-resident clients; foreign retainers invoiced from the IC are outside Vanuatu VAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input VAT recoverable on local business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only VAT on locally incurred costs directly attributable to Vanuatu taxable supplies; offshore media-buying costs are not creditable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net VAT payable or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund is subject to VRC review; the IC must maintain full local documentary trail and a Vanuatu bank account if a refund is claimed.
Must be signed electronically by an authorised local representative with a valid VRC e-services credential.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty plus daily surcharge (approx. VUV 5,000 plus VUV 1,000 per day); late payment: interest at 2% per month; VAT evasion: civil penalty up to 150% of the tax under the VAT Act [Cap. 248], with directors and officers exposed to prosecution and custodial sentencing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Vanuatu imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by an International Company. Dividends may be declared in USD or any foreign currency and paid gros to non-resident shareholders without VRC involvement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable. Vanuatu has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network and no domestic TRC (Tax Residence Certificate) regime. Because the domestic dividend WHT rate is 0%, no treaty relief application is required. For foreign shareholders subject to CFC/GILTI or Subpart F rules (US, UK, Australia, EU), the practical protocol is: (i) obtain a VFSC Certificate of Good Standing; (ii) obtain a substance letter from the registered agent evidencing board management in Port Vila; (iii) retain board minutes approving the dividend and audited financial statements; and (iv) preserve wire transfer records to support foreign tax credit positions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory and 0% under any potential treaty framework - Vanuatu levies no withholding tax on outbound royalties (including PR brand/trademark licences, media analytics IP, and communication technology licences) and no withholding tax on debt interest. There is also no thin-capitalisation or interest-netting rule in Vanuatu, so a related-party loan to the IC is not restricted by local law; however, excessive interest deductions may be disregarded by the foreign parent's tax authority.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Local File or Master File regime is legislated in Vanuatu, and VFSC does not require a transfer pricing study for the annual licence. However, where the IC books intercompany PR retainer, media placement, or crisis communication revenue exceeding VUV 10,000,000 (approx. USD 85,000) per annum, the foreign parent's CFC/GILTI tax authority will apply its own transfer pricing and economic substance tests; a contemporaneous OECD-based TP documentation set should therefore be prepared and updated annually.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP - Comparable Uncontrolled Price for media placement and per-hour PR retainer benchmarking
Resale Price Method for buy-resell PR distribution and press-release licensing models
Cost Plus Method for cost-based service fee arrangements (monitoring, analytics, reporting)
TNMM - Transactional Net Margin Method for routine agency and communication management functions
Profit Split Method for integrated worldwide PR campaigns, joint IP, and shared media analytics
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Following the November 2019 OECD FHTP review, Vanuatu applies economic substance expectations to International Companies generating geographically mobile income, including marketing, public relations, consultancy, and communication strategy services. For the IC to defend its 0% tax position, the core functions - strategic direction, client relationship management, media content approval, and board oversight - must be genuinely performed in Vanuatu with local employees on payroll, a physical office in Port Vila, regular board meetings at the registered office, and records of operational control. VFSC may request an annual substance declaration and financial statements demonstrating that the IC is not a bare nominee shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating the IC solely to invoice global PR retainers and media commissions from related group companies while all personnel, strategy, and client management occur in the US/EU/Australia and the IC maintains no office, no employees, and no real management in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: VFSC strike-off and dissolution under s.121 IC Act [Cap. 222]; adverse FHTP/EU listing status. Foreign: Subpart F/GILTI/CFC inclusion of the full retained profit, IRC s.482 reallocation with penalties up to 40% of the understated foreign tax, denial of treaty benefits, and potential criminal tax evasion referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling shareholders are jointly and severally liable for recharacterised foreign taxes and penalties; courts may issue worldwide asset freezing orders, travel bans, and director disqualification orders; in egregious cases custodial sentences of up to 25 years apply under foreign money laundering statutes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing PR retainer payments from sanctioned individuals, government-linked clients, or opaque third parties through the Vanuatu IC bank account without resident agent KYC, beneficial ownership verification, or reporting of suspicious transactions under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2017.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: corporate fines up to VUV 100,000,000 (approx. USD 850,000), confiscation of assets, loss of banking correspondence relationships, and VFSC revocation of the IC licence; foreign banks may terminate correspondent arrangements and report the IC to FATF-aligned FIUs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners face individual fines up to VUV 100,000,000 and/or imprisonment for money laundering offenses (up to 25 years); travel bans and passport surrenders are routinely imposed during pending FIU investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion via artificial profit shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing inflated invoices for so-called crisis communication and media-monitoring services that are wholly performed by the foreign affiliate's own staff, thereby stripping taxable profit from the operating country into the zero-tax Vanuatu IC without any pricing justification or substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: prosecution for fraudulent misrepresentation to VFSC, fine, and deregistration. Foreign: 100% CFC/GILTI inclusion, transfer pricing adjustment, penalty equal to 100% of the tax on the shifted profit, and foreign criminal tax evasion charges where the invoices are found to be sham documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the sham retainer agreements are personally liable for civil restitution of shifted taxes, subject to travel bans, extradition requests, and imprisonment in the operating country; Vanuatu courts may also enforce foreign revenue judgment debts in certain mutual assistance channels.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed local business activity / VAT evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC providing PR and communication services to Vanuatu-resident tourism, hospitality, or government clients without registering for VAT, without charging the prevailing 15% VAT, and without the required business licence status for domestic operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VRC: retroactive VAT registration, penalty of 100% of the evaded VAT, interest at 2% per month, and prosecution under the VAT Act [Cap. 248]; Ministry of Finance business licence fines; the IC loses its offshore exempt character.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The resident director responsible for the company's administration is personally assessed for the unpaid VAT and may be imprisoned for up to 2 years; the IC's offshore tax exemption is revoked retroactively.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False declaration to VFSC / non-payment of annual fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false beneficial ownership or business activity declarations to VFSC, concealing a change of registered agent, or allowing the annual licence fee to fall into persistent arrears while invoices continue to issue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VFSC deregistration and dissolution; fines up to VUV 50,000,000 (approx. USD 425,000) for false declarations; all contracts issued in the IC's name after strike-off are void, causing unsecured creditor claims against the foreign group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors continuing to trade after strike-off are personally liable for the company's post-dissolution debts, may be disqualified from acting as directors in Vanuatu, and face criminal fines and imprisonment for fraudulent trading; travel bans are available to facilitate enforcement.
